correctness.rationale: Every length-8 reversal-invariant binary dictionary is a union of reversal orbits. The 256 words form 136 orbits, of which 56 are individually comma-free (12 singleton,44 size-two). Pairwise orbit compatibility yields a 56-vertex 929-edge graph; any valid dictionary corresponds to a weighted clique. Independently enumerated ALL 2107 maximal cliques by bitset Bron–Kerbosch; largest weight is 18 with 16 pairwise-eligible maxima. Pairwise compatibility is not sufficient, so every candidate maximum was checked against every proper splice of all ordered codeword pairs. Exactly 12 genuine size-18 dictionaries survive, with 6 palindromes and six reversal pairs each, exchanged in 6 distinct complement pairs. Finite domain is exhaustively covered, not a timeout heuristic; independently computed witness fingerprints match bundled list.

originality.rationale: Churchill 2009 introduces W_r(k,n) for reversal-closed comma-free words, gives general upper bounds, including even k, and constructions at other parameters. Its full article does not report all twelve labeled size-18 binary length-8 codes. Fimmel et al 2023 full paper counts length-two and length-three codes and investigates alphabet self-complementation, a different involution. Wang–Tonchev 2009 addresses generic comma-free searches, but only its abstract was accessible; its possible table is explicitly unresolved. No stronger known theorem inspected determines these equality cases.
